paper_identity.title: Association between the rs9131 and rs3806792 polymorphisms of the CXCL2 gene and the risk of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma in a Guangxi population

final_report_expectations.research_question: Whether CXCL2 rs9131 and rs3806792 polymorphisms are associated with risk of chronic hepatitis B, HBV-related liver cirrhosis, or HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma in Chinese individuals from Guangxi.
final_report_expectations.study_design: Hospital-based case-control genetic association study comparing healthy controls with CHB, HBV-related LC, and HBV-related HCC groups, including allele, genotype, haplotype, sex subgroup, and 1000 Genomes population-frequency comparisons.
final_report_expectations.population_or_materials: 147 healthy controls, 138 chronic hepatitis B patients, 137 HBV-related liver cirrhosis patients, and 150 HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma patients; all participants were Chinese individuals from Guangxi province.
methods: Enrolled HBV-related disease cases from the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University from June 2017 to February 2018 and selected healthy volunteers from the same hospital's health examination center.

Confirmed chronic HBV infection for at least 6 months using HBV serology; defined CHB, LC, and HCC using liver enzymes, imaging, laboratory findings, cytology/histology, AFP, CT, or ultrasonography criteria as applicable.
Extracted DNA from peripheral white blood cells and amplified target regions by PCR.
Genotyped CXCL2 rs9131 and rs3806792 using SNaPshot multiplex genotyping and GeneMarker software.
Compared genotype, allele, and haplotype distributions across disease groups vs controls, including sex-stratified analyses and comparison of healthy controls with 1000 Genomes reference populations.
primary_findings: No significant association was found between CXCL2 rs9131 or rs3806792 and CHB, HBV-related LC, or HBV-related HCC in the Guangxi sample.
The negative finding held across allele, genotype, dominant/recessive model, and haplotype comparisons.
Male and female subgroup analyses did not identify significant associations.
The authors concluded that rs9131 and rs3806792 might not contribute to CHB, HBV-related LC, or HCC development in this Guangxi population.
secondary_findings: Baseline sex distributions were not significantly different across groups, but CHB patients were about 10 years younger than controls, LC patients, and HCC patients.
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was satisfied for both SNPs in all four groups.
Strong linkage disequilibrium was observed between rs9131 and rs3806792 across disease-vs-control comparisons.
The C9131-C3806792 haplotype was the major haplotype in all groups, and T9131-T3806792 was second most common.
Healthy-control genotype and allele frequencies were similar to Han Chinese in Beijing but differed from several other 1000 Genomes populations.
sensitivity_analysis: No formal sensitivity analysis was labeled as such.

Robustness-relevant analyses included age/sex-adjusted logistic regression, male and female subgroup analyses, HWE checks, haplotype analysis, and external population-frequency comparison using 1000 Genomes.
Female subgroup details appear to be in Table S1, which was referenced but not present in the local PDF text.
statistical_tests_used: ANOVA was used for continuous variables such as age across groups.
Chi-square tests and Fisher exact tests were used for categorical variables and allele/genotype frequency comparisons.
Goodness-of-fit chi-square tests assessed Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
Binary logistic regression estimated odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusted for age and sex where appropriate.
SHEsis software estimated linkage disequilibrium and haplotype frequencies.
IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 was used for statistical analyses; two-sided p < 0.05 threshold.
interpretation: The report should present this as a negative genetic association study in a Guangxi Chinese population.
Population-frequency differences vs 1000 Genomes groups should be treated as genetic-background context, not as evidence of disease risk in other ethnicities.
The findings do not rule out CXCL2 biology in HBV-related HCC, other CXCL2 variants, expression-level effects, or associations in larger/multicenter cohorts.
limitations: Relatively small sample size may limit power to detect smaller genetic effects.
Population was geographically and ethnically limited to Chinese individuals from Guangxi.
Only two CXCL2 polymorphism sites were evaluated.
The study did not establish whether rs9131 or rs3806792 affects CXCL2 expression or serum levels.

final_report_expectations.supplement_availability: The article states that additional supporting information may be found online. The local PDF text references Table S1 for female subgroup analyses but does not include the supporting table; online supporting information was not reviewed. The article states datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
uniqueness: Negative association benchmark requiring careful avoidance of false-positive genetic conclusions.
Covers an HBV disease-progression spectrum from CHB to LC to HCC.
Combines SNP genotype/allele models, haplotypes, sex subgroups, HWE checks, and population-genetic comparison.

critical_claims.claim: The study compared healthy controls, CHB patients, HBV-related LC patients, and HBV-related HCC patients from Guangxi.
The two CXCL2 variants tested were rs9131, a 3 prime UTR variant, and rs3806792, an upstream transcript variant, genotyped using SNaPshot.
critical_claims.source_anchor: Introduction; DNA extraction and SNP genotypes

critical_claims.claim: No significant rs9131 or rs3806792 allele or genotype associations were found for CHB, HBV-related LC, or HBV-related HCC compared with healthy controls.
critical_claims.source_anchor: Association between CXCL2 SNPs and risk of HBV-related HCC; Table 2

critical_claims.claim: Haplotype analysis found strong linkage disequilibrium but no significant haplotype-distribution differences between disease groups and controls.
Healthy Guangxi controls had rs9131 and rs3806792 frequencies similar to Han Chinese in Beijing but significantly different from CEU, GIH, JPT, and YRI 1000 Genomes populations.

report_should_not_claim: Do not claim rs9131 or rs3806792 increases or decreases HBV-related HCC risk in the Guangxi sample.
Do not treat ethnic allele-frequency differences as disease-risk evidence.
Do not generalize the negative result to all populations or all CXCL2 variation.
Do not imply CXCL2 expression or serum levels were measured.
Do not claim the online supporting information was reviewed unless retrieved separately.
scoring_focus: Reward accurate negative-association framing and preservation of all four group counts.
Require correct SNP identities, genotyping method, and adjusted logistic-regression/statistical framework.
Check that subgroup/haplotype/population-comparison analyses are included without overinterpretation.
Penalize any fabricated positive association, expression result, or external-risk inference.
